outline.description: Introduces the need for controllable language models, reviews existing alignment methods, and sets the stage for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
subtopics: Why steer large language models?
Limitations of unsupervised pre‑training
Overview of RLHF and its components
Challenges of reinforcement learning for LMs (complexity, instability, computational cost)
Goal of a simpler, more stable alignment method

outline.description: Presents the theoretical foundations underlying preference data, reward modelling, and the Bradley‑Terry / Plackett‑Luce frameworks.
subtopics: Human preference data as pairwise comparisons
Bradley‑Terry model derivation and interpretation
Extension to Plackett‑Luce ranking
Reward function vs. preference distribution
Equivalence classes of reward functions

outline.description: Describes the three‑stage RLHF process (SFT, reward modelling, RL fine‑tuning) and the KL‑constrained objective used in practice.
subtopics: Supervised fine‑tuning (SFT) of a pretrained LM
Collecting preference pairs and fitting a reward model
Maximum‑likelihood reward model loss
KL‑constrained reward maximisation objective
Policy optimisation with PPO / REINFORCE
Practical issues: partition function, reward normalisation, KL‑penalty

outline.description: Shows step‑by‑step how DPO is obtained from the RLHF objective by a change of variables that eliminates the explicit reward model.
subtopics: Optimal policy for the KL‑constrained RL problem
Re‑parameterising the reward in terms of policy and reference model
Cancellation of the partition function in the Bradley‑Terry likelihood
Derivation of the DPO loss (Eq. 8)
Interpretation of the DPO gradient and importance weighting
Algorithmic pipeline: data collection → reference model → DPO optimisation

outline.description: Provides formal analysis of why DPO is sound, its relationship to reward equivalence, and why it avoids instability of actor‑critic methods.
subtopics: Equivalence relation on reward functions
Lemma: same preference distribution within an equivalence class
Lemma: same optimal policy within an equivalence class
Theorem: any reward class can be expressed as β·log(π/π_ref)
Proof sketch and intuition
Comparison with actor‑critic / PPO instability
Role of the soft value (normalisation) term

outline.description: Guides readers through turning the DPO equations into a working training loop, including model initialization, hyper‑parameters, and computational considerations.
subtopics: Choosing and initializing the reference policy (π_ref)
Handling unavailable SFT models
Batching, token‑level log‑probabilities, and numerical stability
Hyper‑parameter β and its effect on KL‑constraint
Training schedule, optimizer choices, and early stopping
Implementation tricks: caching π_ref log‑probs, mixed‑precision
Comparison of compute cost vs. PPO

outline.description: Analyzes DPO on a synthetic sentiment‑control task, focusing on reward‑KL trade‑offs and comparison with baselines.
subtopics: Task definition and data generation using a sentiment classifier
Baselines: SFT, PPO, PPO‑GT, Unlikelihood, Preferred‑FT, Best‑of‑N
Measuring reward (sentiment score) and sequence‑level KL
Results: frontier plots and interpretation
Why DPO dominates PPO and even PPO‑GT

outline.description: Presents results on real human‑preference datasets (Reddit TL;DR and Anthropic Helpful‑Harmless), evaluation methodology, and performance analysis.
subtopics: Datasets and preprocessing
Reference model creation for each task
Evaluation metrics: GPT‑4 win‑rate, temperature sweeps, human study
Comparison of DPO with PPO, Preferred‑FT, Best‑of‑N, zero‑shot prompts
Robustness to sampling temperature and hyper‑parameter choices
Analysis of convergence speed and stability

outline.description: Examines how DPO‑trained policies transfer to unseen domains, contrasting with PPO‑trained models.
subtopics: OOD test on CNN/DailyMail after TL;DR training
Quantitative win‑rate results
Discussion of why DPO may retain or improve generalisation
Limitations of current OOD experiments and future probes

outline.description: Explores the relationship between GPT‑4 automated judgments and human ratings, and discusses best practices for evaluation.
subtopics: Design of the human study (pairwise comparisons, raters, instructions)
Prompt engineering for GPT‑4 (simple vs. concise)
Correlation analysis between GPT‑4 and human agreement
Implications for using LLMs as evaluators
Guidelines for future evaluation of preference‑based training

outline.description: Summarises the impact of DPO, highlights remaining challenges, and outlines promising research avenues.
subtopics: Recap of DPO’s advantages (simplicity, stability, compute)
Open questions on OOD generalisation and reward over‑optimisation
Scaling DPO to very large models
Self‑labeling and semi‑supervised extensions
Applying DPO beyond text (vision, audio, multimodal generation)
Potential integration with other alignment tools (constitutional AI, safety guards)
